_comment_server_id: Must be unique across everything reading this server's binlog, because
MySQL treats a CDC reader as a replica and two replicas sharing a
server_id kick each other off in a loop. The database itself is 1, so
this takes a number far away from anything a real replica would pick.
_comment_snapshot: schema_only, not initial. An initial snapshot would replay every row
already in outbox_event - which for this table means republishing every
event the polling relay has ever delivered. The rows are a log of what
was already sent, so streaming from now is the correct starting point,
and it is also why this comparison can be run without wiping the table.
_comment_schema_history: Debezium stores the table's DDL history in Kafka so it can interpret old
binlog entries after a schema change. RF 3 for the same reason as every
other internal topic here: a connector whose history lives on one broker
cannot recover when that broker dies, which is the exact test phase 6
_comment_router: The EventRouter SMT is what turns a row change into a domain event. It
unwraps the Debezium envelope, publishes the payload column as the
message body, and keys by aggregate_id - the same paymentId key the
polling relay uses, so per-payment ordering holds in both arms.
Without this, consumers would receive Debezium's change envelope -
before/after/source/op - and every consumer would need to know it was
reading a MySQL row rather than a payment event. The CDC arm would then
be a different contract rather than a different delivery mechanism, and
_comment_traceparent: Phase 6g. The trace context, from the row to a Kafka header, so the CDC
arm carries it exactly like the polling relay does. Format is
column:placement:alias - `header` puts it on the record, `envelope`
would put it in the payload where a consumer would have to parse it out.
Debezium HAS a native version of this: set tracing.span.context.field and
the SMT will continue the trace itself, producing a Debezium span in the
middle. It is not used here, and the reason is a dependency rather than a
preference - it needs the OpenTelemetry API on the Connect worker's
classpath, which means either a custom image or a plugin drop into a
container this project otherwise runs unmodified. Copying the column into
the header gets the trace across the boundary, which is what the phase
asked for; what it gives up is a span for the CDC hop itself, so the
waterfall shows the request, then the consume, with the binlog latency
as an unexplained gap rather than a labelled one.
The polling relay makes the opposite trade: it opens its own publish span
because it is JVM code that can. That difference is a real one to name in
the CDC-vs-polling comparison and it did not exist before this phase.
_comment_topic: A SEPARATE topic from the polling relay's, deliberately. Both arms can
then run at once against the same outbox table and be compared on the
same traffic, rather than on two runs at two different times. Pointing
them at one topic would double-publish every event and measure nothing.
_comment_tombstones: Off. The router emits a tombstone when a row is deleted, and nothing
deletes outbox rows here - but a future retention job would, and a
tombstone for a payment event would read downstream as 'this payment
_comment_route_by: route.by.field is REQUIRED even when the topic is a fixed string. The SMT
defaults it to `aggregatetype`, Debezium's own outbox convention, and fails
the record with `aggregatetype is not a valid field name` against any table
that does not use their column names. The connector reports RUNNING while
every record dies in the transform - a healthy-looking pipeline publishing
nothing, which is the same shape of failure phase 4 found in the OTLP
